re_line: AUKUS CBO fight: Marles says "they are wrong" · Wong to elevate AI as security threat · Pacific Resilience Facility at $200m of $500m · Cook Islands cyclone relief sails Monday · Newspoll: Taylor now preferred PM
morning_memo: Richard Marles rejected a US Congressional Budget Office finding that selling Virginia-class submarines to Australia could shrink the US Navy's attack submarine fleet through 2060, calling the assessment wrong on ABC's Insiders.

Penny Wong will tell parliament on Tuesday that artificial intelligence is now a major foreign policy and national security challenge, citing Iranian and Russian disinformation operations aimed at democracies.

Palau's Surangel Whipps Jr., chair of the Pacific Islands Forum, said the Pacific Resilience Facility has crossed $200 million of its $500 million capitalization target at COP31, with Andrew Forrest's Minderoo Foundation pledging $5 million.

top_stories.headline: Marles rejects US budget office warning on AUKUS submarine deal
top_stories.body: **Richard Marles** rejected a US Congressional Budget Office report warning that the sale of Virginia-class submarines to Australia could diminish the US Navy's attack submarine force through to 2060. "They are wrong," the deputy prime minister said in televised remarks, adding that AUKUS "is very much happening" and that the American production rate "is absolutely increasing". Canberra has committed *$368 billion* over three decades to the programme, Reuters reported.
top_stories.src_line: per Reuters: "Australia criticises US Congressional Budget Office over AUKUS comments" · also ABC News

top_stories.headline: Wong to declare AI a top national security challenge
top_stories.body: **Penny Wong** will tell parliament on Tuesday that artificial intelligence is a "major foreign policy and national security challenge", warning that the technology hands foreign actors new tools to disrupt democracies. She will cite an Iranian operation using fake journalist personas to sway opinion on the US-Iran conflict, and Russian covert use of AI-generated deepfakes in US elections. The speech comes amid concern that AI data centres built in Australia could be vulnerable to foreign actors.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News: "Foreign minister to elevate AI as national security challenge"

top_stories.headline: Pacific Resilience Facility passes $200 million toward COP31 goal
top_stories.body: The Pacific Resilience Facility launched its international capitalization campaign at COP31 in Antalya, crossing *$200 million* of a $500 million target, said **Surangel Whipps Jr.**, Palau's president and chair of the Pacific Islands Forum. Of that, $100 million is Pacific money. Andrew Forrest's Minderoo Foundation pledged $5 million. "We should not have to pay for our own survival, but we act without hesitation," Whipps said, calling for the remaining $300 million before the next COP.
top_stories.src_line: per Pacific Island Times: "'Finance delayed is finance denied': Pacific leaders push for climate pledges"

overnight_items.headline: Marles plays down Trump AI data centre threat
overnight_items.body_text: **Richard Marles** played down a Trump administration threat concerning AI data centres in his Sunday broadcast appearance. The exchange ran alongside his rejection of the Congressional Budget Office submarine assessment, placing both the alliance's technology and its undersea files in the same interview.

overnight_items.headline: Spy chief warns of data centre and AI risks
overnight_items.body_text: Australia's intelligence chief warned of security risks attached to data centres and artificial intelligence, Bloomberg reported, citing The Age. The warning precedes **Penny Wong**'s parliamentary speech on AI as a national security problem and follows reporting on foreign exposure in Australia's data centre buildout.

overnight_items.headline: Chinese businessman recruits Daniel Andrews as adviser while touting data centre ambitions
overnight_items.body_text: Lewis Jin has recruited former Victorian premier **Daniel Andrews** as an adviser on property deals, the Sydney Morning Herald reported, while separately promoting ambitions to advance China's strategic interest in Australia's data centre boom. The report lands the same weekend Canberra elevated data centre security into its foreign policy messaging.

overnight_items.headline: Newspoll: Taylor overtakes Albanese as preferred prime minister
overnight_items.body_text: Voters have lost faith in **Anthony Albanese** and now prefer Opposition Leader **Angus Taylor** as prime minister, The Australian reported from its latest Newspoll. The masthead also published an explainer on how Newspoll now measures the preferred prime minister question across Albanese, Taylor, and Pauline Hanson.

overnight_items.headline: Grattan urges Canberra to underwrite the last two refineries past 2030
overnight_items.body_text: The Grattan Institute called on the federal government to underwrite the Geelong and Brisbane refineries beyond 2030 as fuel reserves run down, saying Australia is "dangerously exposed" on fuel imports. The Australian Financial Review carried the same warning. Liquid fuel security has sat unresolved alongside Australia's defence posture decisions.

overnight_items.headline: New Zealand exporters push back as Washington probes lamb imports
overnight_items.body_text: Atkins Ranch chief executive **Pat Maher** said New Zealand sheepmeat is "complementary" to US-grown lamb as American officials investigate imports to protect the domestic industry. The United States harvests two million lambs a year, Maher said, and lamb is under four percent of American meat sales. Australian and New Zealand sheepmeat industries both face the scrutiny.

pacific_wire.headline: Nassau state of emergency holds as Xavier weakens
pacific_wire.body_text: The Cook Islands government said the state of emergency for Nassau remains in force as Tropical Cyclone Xavier continues to weaken. Residents across Pukapuka, Nassau, and Manihiki are safe, with coastal damage reported and assessments underway in the Northern Group.

pacific_wire.headline: Patrol boat Te Kukupa II to carry cyclone relief north on Monday
pacific_wire.body_text: The Cook Islands Police patrol boat Te Kukupa II will sail for Nassau and Pukapuka on Monday, weather permitting, with *22 people* aboard including two doctors and a mechanic. The barge Taunga Nui is loaded and waiting on safe passage.

pacific_wire.headline: Samoa under wind and marine warnings as Xavier tracks southwest
pacific_wire.body_text: The Samoa Meteorological Service said Tropical Cyclone Xavier, now Category 1, sat about 730 kilometres northeast of Apia and could enter Samoa's 400-kilometre radius by Monday. Wind and marine warnings remain in force nationwide. Xavier reached Category 5 on Wednesday before weakening.

pacific_wire.headline: Questions mount over $4.5 million tala missing from Samoa Ports Authority
pacific_wire.body_text: A Samoa Observer letter demands the FAST government explain a reported *$4.5 million tala* in public funds missing from the Samoa Ports Authority, paid to an overseas recipient. No statement has come from the Prime Minister's office. The writer warned donors to examine how their assistance is being managed.

pacific_wire.headline: Australian intelligence agency urges Fiji to get ahead of meth and cocaine
pacific_wire.body_text: Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission national manager **Wendy Darling** told Fijian officials that Australia consumed *15.8 tonnes* of methamphetamine and almost eight tonnes of cocaine in the year to August 2025, generating an estimated AU$13.8 billion in criminal proceeds. She urged wastewater monitoring and stronger inter-agency cooperation before Fiji faces comparable harm.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji national ID to stay voluntary under bill due in parliament
pacific_wire.body_text: The National Identification Bill 2026 would create a voluntary identity system with safeguards on biometric data including fingerprints and facial images, and bars denial of services to the unregistered. The steering committee chaired by Minister for Policing and Communications **Ioane Naivalurua** endorsed the draft on November 20. The bill is expected during the sitting from November 30 to December 4.

pacific_wire.headline: Australia launches Bougainville water project serving nearly 1,000 people
pacific_wire.body_text: Australian High Commissioner **Jamie Isbister** launched a community water and sanitation project at Noupan, North Bougainville, installing 20 large rainwater tanks and two improved toilets for about *940 people*. The ward had faced years of shortages.

pacific_wire.headline: Maladina rejects claim Papua LNG collapses when licence expires
pacific_wire.body_text: Petroleum Minister **Jimmy Maladina** said claims the Papua LNG Project faces collapse when Petroleum Retention Licence No.15 expires on November 30 are misleading. The dispute is with Kerenga Kua, who raised the expiry.

pacific_wire.headline: New Zealand police commissioner praises Vaka Puaikura police post
pacific_wire.body_text: New Zealand Police Commissioner **Richard Chambers** praised the community effort behind the Vaka Puaikura police post, citing its role in local policing and in ties between the Cook Islands and New Zealand Police.

pacific_wire.headline: Ditoka says reopened Brussels embassy will serve the European diaspora
pacific_wire.body_text: Minister for Foreign Affairs and External Trade **Sakiasi Ditoka** said the reopened Fijian embassy in Brussels will widen consular access for Fijians across Europe, speaking at a talanoa with diaspora members. The reopening followed nearly five decades of EU engagement.

new_zealand.headline: Turnout tracking toward second lowest in New Zealand history
new_zealand.body_text: Voter turnout at this election is on course to be the second lowest on record, RNZ reported, with criticism of negative campaigning feeding questions about disengagement from the electoral process. 1News ran the same finding.

new_zealand.headline: 'Wildly naive': Is New Zealand sleepwalking into a world of war?
new_zealand.body_text: The Post asks whether New Zealand is underprepared for a deteriorating strategic environment, carrying the charge that current settings are "wildly naive". The piece follows the New Zealand Defence Force database compromise reported earlier in the week.

canberra_politics.headline: Albanese's office is the biggest and best paid in 13 years
canberra_politics.body_text: **Anthony Albanese** has hired more staff than Scott Morrison, Malcolm Turnbull, and Tony Abbott, with the share on top salaries rising sharply, the Sydney Morning Herald found. Crossbench staffing allocations have been cut over the same period.

canberra_politics.headline: Labor polling shows One Nation leading the Coalition 49-32 in Mildura
canberra_politics.body_text: One Nation leads the Coalition *49 to 32* on the primary vote in Mildura, according to Labor polling reported by The Australian, which also found One Nation topping the primary vote in three Coalition-held seats ahead of the Victorian election.

canberra_politics.headline: Victorian Labor MPs call leadership change 'a disaster'
canberra_politics.body_text: Victorian Labor MPs described the party's leadership change as "a disaster" in a campaign pre-mortem reported by the ABC. The recriminations run as Labor's own polling shows One Nation eroding the Coalition primary vote in regional seats.

canberra_politics.headline: Butler orders parliamentary inquiry into peptide prescribing
canberra_politics.body_text: Health Minister **Mark Butler** ordered an inquiry into peptide prescription and use, citing escalating Therapeutic Goods Administration reports of unapproved peptides supplied through telehealth and dispensaries. Consultation hearings begin this month, with a final report due mid-2027. The Sydney Morning Herald reported the inquiry will also examine social media platforms.

canberra_politics.headline: Greens candidate considered quitting after swastikas painted on her posters
canberra_politics.body_text: **Talia Gulpilil**, the Greens candidate for the regional Victorian seat of Eildon, nearly withdrew from the state election after her campaign posters were defaced with swastikas, the Guardian reported. She said her ten-year-old daughter saw the vandalism from a school bus before it was removed.

canberra_politics.headline: Victorian Opposition Leader Jess Wilson pledges a fresh start
canberra_politics.body_text: Opposition Leader **Jess Wilson**, one term into her parliamentary career, is campaigning on a fresh start as she seeks the Victorian premiership, the Canberra Times reported.

business_economy.headline: Google cancels funding for 25 Australian news outlets
business_economy.body_text: Google has cancelled funding arrangements covering 25 Australian news outlets, the Australian Financial Review reported, a decision with direct bearing on the news bargaining framework Canberra has used to extract payments from US platforms.

business_economy.headline: Rarotonga petrol and diesel prices rise under new price order
business_economy.body_text: Petrol and diesel prices increased in Rarotonga while liquefied petroleum gas fell, under a new Price Order that took effect. Brent crude closed at *89.95* on November 20, down 3.42 percent.

calendar_watch.event: Wong delivers a major foreign policy speech to parliament on artificial intelligence
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Sets Australia's declared position on AI as a national security and foreign interference problem.

calendar_watch.event: Papua New Guinea's Petroleum Retention Licence No.15 expires
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Determines the next procedural step for the Papua LNG Project after ministerial denials that the project collapses on expiry.

calendar_watch.event: Fiji parliamentary sitting, National Identification Bill 2026 expected
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Would create Fiji's first voluntary national identity and biometric framework.
Labor's own polling shows One Nation leading the Coalition in regional seats, with federal read-through on the Coalition primary vote.

calendar_watch.event: Final report of the federal peptides inquiry
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Will shape regulation of telehealth prescribing and unapproved therapeutic imports.

key_stat.label: Australian commitment to AUKUS over three decades
key_stat.context: Marles cited continuity of the programme while rejecting a Congressional Budget Office finding that Virginia-class sales could shrink the US attack submarine force through 2060.

also_today.headline: Namah invites New Zealanders to Papua New Guinea on new direct flights
also_today.body_text: Tourism Minister **Belden Namah** said new direct flights between Papua New Guinea and New Zealand are expected to bring more New Zealand visitors, and invited them to the country's natural and cultural attractions.

also_today.headline: Australia funds first Pacific athletics coaching academy in Nadi
also_today.body_text: The PacificAus Sports Athletics Coaching Academy opened at Nadi with 41 coaches from 14 Pacific nations for a seven-day programme running November 21 to 28, funded by the Australian government through the PacificAus Sports Brisbane 2032 Games Pathways grant.

also_today.headline: Fiji water authority says Batiki and Ovalau now seeking emergency supply
also_today.body_text: Water Authority of Fiji chief executive **Seru Soderberg** said Batiki Island has sought assistance and requests are now arriving from Ovalau, with rural sources drying well before urban ones. Carting services are running to rural and intermittently supplied urban areas.

also_today.headline: More than 40 Fijian communities apply for borehole grants
also_today.body_text: Minister for Multi-Ethnic Affairs **Charan Jeath Singh** said more than 40 borehole applications have arrived under the ministry's multi-ethnic community grant programme, with grants of $5,000 to $15,000 covering a tank and solar pump. He met Indian High Commissioner **Suneet Mehta** about cheaper Indian-sourced pumps.

also_today.headline: Fiji prosecutor challenges justice ministry to deliver trafficking reforms in six months
also_today.body_text: Deputy Director of Public Prosecutions **John Rabuku** challenged the Ministry of Justice to implement eight human trafficking recommendations within four to six months, naming legal reform, inter-agency cooperation, victim identification procedures, and training as immediate priorities.

also_today.headline: Cook Islands infrastructure secretary appointment expected by year's end
also_today.body_text: Recruitment for a new Infrastructure Cook Islands secretary continues, with the appointment expected to be announced before the end of the year.

opeds_today.headline: Anthony Albanese talks a big game about sovereignty. But Australia remains in thrall to its 'unreliable boyfriend'
opeds_today.central_argument: Sovereignty has become the buzzword of Australian political rhetoric precisely as it has become hardest to define or control.
opeds_today.summary: Schultz argues that Australia depends on US technology platforms for the digital infrastructure of daily life, and asks what happens when those platforms go dark. She links the question to AUKUS, data centres, and intellectual property. Most Australians, she writes, feel unsafe in the world.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Frames the domestic political argument Wong's AI speech will have to answer on Tuesday.
